title: Newcastle United attempting to trademark ‘Howay the lads’ phrase
content:
Newcastle United are attempting to trademark the phrase “Howay the lads”.

In Geordie dialect — the colloquial language used by people local to Newcastle and the surrounding area — “Howay the lads” literally means “come on (or let’s go), boys”.

The club applied to register the iconic words as a trademark with the UK Intellectual Property Office (IPO) on March 14, 2025, two days before their historic Carabao Cup final triumph over Liverpool, which ended a 56-year trophy drought.

Should they be successful, Newcastle would gain exclusive rights under British law to use “Howay the lads” on merchandise for an initial 10-year period, although they can then apply for indefinite renewals. Newcastle would then be able to take legal action against potential infringers and counterfeiters.

Their application covers categories ranging from football shirts — it already features in the club’s kit for 2025-26 — to beers, other alcoholic beverages, soft drinks, lampshades, microwaves, hairdryers and air fresheners.

Opposition to Newcastle’s application has been registered by another party, who are contesting the club’s attempts to trademark the phrase. The process remains ongoing, with Newcastle attempting to convince the IPO they should be awarded the trademark.

The move, while commercially savvy and seemingly an attempt to capitalise on the success of Eddie Howe’s team on the pitch, given it was lodged just before last year’s Wembley final, may prove controversial.

“Howay the lads” may be closely associated with Newcastle United Football Club itself, but it also has wider Geordie significance and is used as a rallying cry by supporters towards the team. Should the club gain the trademark, then other companies who produce Newcastle United-related memorabilia and retail products, including small local firms, would be unable to use the phrase on their own goods.

Those words are emblazoned above the inside of the tunnel at St James’ Park, with both sets of players walking down the steps under “Howay the lads” to get out on to the pitch, an image which is regularly picked up by TV cameras and broadcast to global audiences.

For 2025-26, the phrase also features on the back of the neck of the men’s home shirt.

Interestingly, “Howay the lasses” features on the back of the women’s home shirt for this season, with Newcastle already having successfully been awarded the decade-long trademark for that phrase. The club lodged both applications on the same date, but there was no opposition to “Howay the Lasses” and it was registered by the IPO on August 15, 2025.

Trademarking names and phrases is a normal business practice, which sports clubs regularly do with iconic imagery, phrasing and logos.

In 2019, for example, Liverpool FC controversially attempted to trademark the name “Liverpool” within the context of all club merchandise but were unsuccessful.

Newcastle declined to comment.
